audit_status.source_base: Hebrew/Aramaic source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Restored, source-grounded draft of Ezra 2 following Hebrew witness; preserves names, numbers, and ritual-notes. Counts mirror KJV numbering but remain flagged for witness verification where numeric or name-variants occur.

verses.restored: Now these are the children of the province who went up from the exile, those whom Nebuchadnezzar (Hebrew נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר) king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his city.

familiar.text: Now these are the children of the province that went up out of the captivity, of those which had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon, and came again unto Jerusalem and Judah, every one unto his city;

verses.restored: These sought their registration among those reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found; therefore they were excluded from the priesthood.

familiar.text: These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Exclusion due to absence from genealogical rolls; 'polluted' in tradition implies ritual impurity, not moral judgement alone.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Tirshatha = Persian governor; Urim and Thummim denote accepted cultic decision devices.

translation_notes: Divine name in source rendered as YHWH (Hebrew יהוה) where present (v.68).
Genealogical names follow Hebrew forms; numerals preserved from source but many ancient totals show textual variance — see audit flags.
Tirshatha (v.63) is a Persian-era official title; 'Nethinim' retained as a group-name reflecting cultic service.
safety_note: This chapter lists servile groups, ritual exclusion, and population counts; treat identity data carefully and avoid modern targeting.
source_witness_audit_flags: numeric_totals require cross-check with Nehemiah 7 and Masoretic/Qumran/LXX witnesses
name-variant forms (e.g., Nebuchadnezzar/Nebuchadrezzar, Tirshatha) need palaeographic check
several family names may be duplicated or conflated across traditions
